newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia diesel supported by demand, MidEast shutdowns.
newsitem.headline: Asia diesel supported by demand, MidEast shutdowns.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps dipped slightly on Friday despite a sharp drop on crude and oil product prices in the West with renewed Asian demand and shutdowns at three Middle East refineries providing support, industry sources said.

The higher Singapore gas oil prices over western values have attracted arbitrage cargoes from the U.S. West Coast with about three to four 30,000-tonne cargoes fixed for shipment to East Asia for arrival in December, traders said.
November gas oil swaps opened to trade at a low of $29.90 before picking up in active trade with deals at $30.00, $30.10 and $30.20, down slightly from Thursday's close of $30.45/30.65, brokers said.
It was last quoted at $30.25/30.35, they said.
The fall was modest when compared with the overnight fall of 93 cents per barrel on NYMEX crude for December to $23.35, and a 2.01-cent drop in heating oil prices to 66.85 cents a gallon.

Traders said the market's resilience was due to China's return to the market this week to buy one 30,000-tonne cargo and one 15,000-tonne parcel at between $236 and $238 per tonne on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis.
This is in addition to the large volumes sold on an ex-terminal basis in Hong Kong, they said.
The market is also seeing increased purchases from Indonesia which had already almost doubled its purchases for November to between four and five million barrels.
"Indonesia is rumored to the in the market for another one million barrel for November," one trader told Reuters earlier.
Steady prices were also attributed to a larger-than-expected purchase by India for December arrival of about 520,000-tonnes.
Prices were also supported by scheduled maintenances of at least two refineries in the Middle East.
The 305,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Jubail refinery in Saudi Arabia is due for maintenance in November for about a month.
Jubail is operated by Saudi Aramco Shell Refinery Co (Sasref), a joint venture between state-owned Aramco and Royal Dutch Shell Group
A 170,00-bpd crude distillation unit (CDU) at Kuwait's Mina al-Ahmadi 420,000-bpd refinery will also be shut for maintenance on November 3 for three weeks, traders said.
The Mina al-Ahmadi refinery is a major exporter of middle distillates.
Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) has also scheduled a three-week maintenance at its 135,000-bpd Ruwais CDU in mid-November, traders said.
